speaker: Doctor
text: To understand the nature of your wrist pain and limited hand movement, can you tell me if this injury happened suddenly after a specific event or if it developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history; given the radiation of pain to the elbow and your mother's history with rheumatoid arthritis, are you experiencing any morning stiffness in your hands that lasts more than 30 minutes? REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Patient
text: patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any visible swelling, redness, or warmth in your right wrist or thumb base, and does the pain specifically worsen when you extend your wrist against resistance? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Wrist, X-Ray Right Hand. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your imaging and blood work are normal, but the pain radiates to your elbow and worsens with lifting your child, does the pain specifically worsen when you rotate your forearm or lift your thumb against resistance?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previous fall on right outstretched hand six months ago. No significant other medical history. Social history: Patient is a mother of an infant, leading a relatively active lifestyle. Does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal imaging and lack of inflammatory markers, but significant pain with lifting your child, do you feel a specific clicking or snapping sensation when you actively lift your thumb away from your palm or wrist? REQUEST TEST: EMG_Nerve_Conduction_Study Right_Ulnar_Nerve, Right_Median_Nerve.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your nerve conduction studies, X-rays, and blood work are all normal, and the pain specifically worsens when lifting your child, do you feel any pain or tenderness when I press on the anatomical snuffbox (the hollow at the base of your thumb)?

speaker: Patient
